summary: Kuito Airport (SVP/FNKU) is a regional airport serving Kuito, the capital of Bié Province in central Angola. Situated on the Angolan Central Plateau at roughly 1,680 meters above sea level, it provides essential connectivity for the province and supports both civilian and charter operations. The airport plays a vital role in linking this inland region to Luanda and other Angolan destinations.
faqs:
Q: How far is Kuito Airport from the city center?
A: The airport is located a short drive from central Kuito, typically around 5-10 kilometers depending on the route taken.

Q: Which airlines operate flights to Kuito Airport?
A: Domestic carriers such as TAAG Angola Airlines and regional operators serve Kuito with scheduled and charter flights, primarily connecting to Luanda.

Q: Is the airport open to international flights?
A: Kuito primarily handles domestic flights; international travelers typically connect through Luanda's Quatro de Fevereiro Airport.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a medium-sized regional airport, it offers basic passenger terminal services including a waiting area, check-in counters, and limited concessions.
transport_tips: Taxis are the most common way to reach the airport from Kuito city center, and it's advisable to arrange transport in advance as ride-hailing apps are not widely available in the region. Hotel staff can typically help book a reliable driver. Roads from central Kuito to the airport are generally paved but allow extra time during the rainy season.
local_tip: Kuito sits at high altitude on the Angolan plateau, so even short flights can involve notable weather changes — pack a light layer as mornings and evenings can be cool year-round.
